 The Chicago Bulls look to get back on track Wednesday night when they visit the Brooklyn Nets . Both rebuilding teams have identical records, with Chicago having suffered one more loss in conference action.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Last time out, the Bulls couldn't make it three wins in a row at Cleveland , falling 126-115 to the Cavaliers. Chicago led by six after the first quarter before its offense stalled in the second, allowing Cleveland to take control. Donovan "Spida" Mitchell scored 30 of his 39 points after halftime, including 20 in the fourth quarter, to put the game away. Norman Powell led Chicago with 27 points, while Matas Buzelis added 23.
 The Bulls are 3-10 and will look to regroup Wednesday in Brooklyn.
 Powell leads Chicago with 21.6 points per game. Over the last three games, he's averaging 28 points per game while making 10 or more buckets in each contest.
 Josh Giddey averages 8.5 assists per game to lead the squad. He's posted at least seven games with eight or more assists so far this season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement One story line to watch: the potential, albeit limited, for a Nic Claxton revenge game. The 27-year-old center came to Chicago from Brooklyn in an offseason four-team trade that also sent Julius Randle to the Nets from the Timberwolves . A change-of-scenery candidate, Claxton has come off the bench in four appearances while managing a left hamstring injury that has caused him to miss nine games. He's averaging just under eight points per game and 4.5 rebounds per game.
 Claxton grabbed a Nets season-best 14 boards against Chicago last January.
 Michael Porter Jr. leads the nets in both points per game (21.8) and rebounds per game (7.4) this season. Randle is averaging 20.9 points per game and dishing out just under five assists per game.
